# trafficserver / fuzz_proxy_protocol

trafficserver's own fuzz target `fuzz_proxy_protocol` ([source](source/fuzz_proxy_protocol.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over trafficserver (apache/trafficserver at 97d2831f).

Views the input (size_data from 8 to 1024 bytes) in place as a swoc::TextView and passes it with a new ProxyProtocol to proxy_protocol_parse, which parses a PROXY protocol v1 or v2 header when the input begins with that version's preface and has at least 15 (v1) or 16 (v2) bytes; it drops the returned length and the parsed fields. Before the call it installs a new Diags object with DiagsPtr::set, and it deletes that object after. It returns -1 for an input with size_data below 8 or above 1024.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against trafficserver at commit 97d2831f with 3 patches to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/fuzz_proxy_protocol.cc is trafficserver 97d2831f's tests/fuzzing/fuzz_proxy_protocol.cc with one Theorem Labs change: its length check returns -1, not 1, for an input outside its limits (libFuzzer rejects the input; the driver exits 0, not 78).

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.
